questions.q: What specific retrieval failure is multi-query RAG built to address?
options: The vector database running out of storage
The relevant content exists in the collection, but its phrasing doesn't closely match the user's query vocabulary
The embedding model producing vectors of the wrong dimensionality
The LLM exceeding its max_tokens limit
questions.explain: Multi-query RAG specifically targets the case where a single query embedding lands too far from the real answer's vocabulary in vector space, even though the answer is genuinely present.

questions.q: What does multi-query RAG actually do with the user's original question?
options: It discards the question and asks the user to rephrase it manually
It uses an LLM to generate several differently-worded reformulations, then retrieves separately for each one
It translates the question into a different language before embedding it
It skips retrieval entirely and answers from the model's training data
questions.explain: Multi-query RAG generates multiple alternative phrasings of the same intent, embeds and retrieves for each one, and combines the results.

questions.q: Why are results from multiple reformulations typically deduplicated by chunk ID?
options: Because vector databases reject duplicate search requests
Because deduplication increases the embedding dimensionality
Because the same genuinely relevant chunk is often retrieved by more than one reformulation
Because chunk IDs expire after one search
questions.explain: Since different reformulations aim at the same underlying intent, they frequently retrieve overlapping chunks, so deduplication avoids feeding the same chunk into the prompt multiple times.

questions.q: What does multi-query RAG cost compared to a single retrieval pass?
options: Nothing extra — it reuses the same embedding and search calls
It replaces the vector database with a graph database
It eliminates the need for re-ranking
It multiplies retrieval cost directly — one embedding call and search per reformulation, plus the LLM call to generate them
questions.explain: Each reformulation requires its own embedding call and vector database search, on top of the initial LLM call that generates the reformulations.

questions.q: When does this lesson suggest multi-query RAG is most worth its added cost?
options: On every single query, regardless of confidence
Only when the vector database has fewer than 100 documents
Only when citations are not required
On queries where first-pass retrieval confidence is already low, or where users are known to phrase questions differently from the source vocabulary
questions.explain: Because multi-query RAG triples retrieval cost, it's suggested as a selective technique for cases where a single query is unlikely to retrieve well on its own, not a default for every query.
